MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  August 16, 2010

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at 5:05
p.m., on August 16, 2010, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on August 11, 2010, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Ledesma (arrived at 5:08 p.m.)
  Council Member Schlicht
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Schlicht

INVOCATION: Council Member Ury

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Attorney Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6.

City Council Minutes  1  August 16, 2010
 CS2. Conference with Real Property Negotiator Government Code Section 54956.8: The
  real property commonly known as The Shops at Mission Viejo (Mall Property) that
  is generally bounded by Crown Valley Parkway to the north, Medical Center Road
  to the east, Marguerite Parkway to the southeast, Via Curacion to the south, and the
  I 5 San Diego Freeway to the west and comprised of Assessor Parcel Nos. (APNs)
  740-011-38, 740-011-39, 740-011-43, 740-011-45, 740-121-15 owned by Mission Viejo
  Associates, L.P., a California limited partnership. CDA Negotiators: On behalf of
  Community Development Agency of the City of Mission Viejo (“CDA”): Dennis
  Wilberg, City Manager/CDA Executive Director, Irwin Bornstein, Assistant City
  Manager, Charles Wilson, Director of Community Development, James Williams,
  Economic Advisor, Celeste Brady, CDA Counsel, and William Curley, III, City
  Attorney. Owner Negotiators: On behalf of Mission Viejo Associates, L.P.
  (“Owner”) from Simon Property Group, the Owner entity’s managing general
  partner: William Hammer and Bruce Moore, Esq. Under negotiation and
  discussion: CDA will consider the proposed price and terms of a real property
  transaction that may be the basis for amendment(s) of the OPA and Covenants
  Agreement (Amendment). The proposed Amendment will address Covenants
  Agreement, a real property interest. Factors Affecting Price and Terms under
  Negotiation: (i) modification, if any, of Covenants Agreement; and (ii) reuse and
  redevelopment of Major Department Store space.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour or 5:08 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:03 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there was no reportable action for Closed Session item
CS1. For item CS2, the City Council received an update and final action will be taken during
agenda item 24 this evening.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize Waste Management for their $4,588.95 Donation to the Friends of the
  Mission Viejo Library

  Mayor Kelley received the donation and presented a Certificate of Appreciation to
  Michelle Clark of Waste Management.

P2.  Recognize Mission Viejo’s Community Recycling Program Award Winner

  Michelle Clarke from Waste Management presented the recycling award to
  representatives of the Heritage Villas Senior Apartment Homes.

City Council Minutes  2  August 16, 2010
 PUBLIC COMMENTS

Joyce Saltzgiver, M.V.: announced that she heard Council Member Schlicht call Mayor Kelley a
liar at the last City Council Meeting and she asked Ms. Schlicht to be civil and set an example.

Larry Maurer, M.V.: speaking on behalf of the Friends of the Mission Viejo Library, he
announced that the 2nd Annual Readers' Festival will be held on Saturday, September 25, 2010.

Joe Holtzman, M.V.: stated that it's a conflict of interest for RJM Design Group to negotiate a
construction easement with American Golf for the potential expansion of the Marguerite Tennis
Center. He also questioned the budget figures Mayor Kelley presented in her Candidate
Statement.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 3, 8, 11, 13, 16 and 17 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate
discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

4.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for May 2010

  Received and filed.

5.  Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report for May 2010

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Community Development  Financing Authority (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for May 2010

City Council Minutes  3  August 16, 2010
   Received and filed.

7.  Check Register dated June 25, 2010, in the amount of $1,792,257.30

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

9.  Check Register dated July 9, 2010, in the amount of $724,134.27

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

10.  Check Register dated July 16, 2010, in the amount of $1, 086,018.12

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

12.  Check Register dated July 30, 2010, in the amount of $1,176,473.44

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

14.  Acceptance of Tract Map 16877 and Associated Bond and Agreement

  (1) Approved Tract Map 16877 and authorized the City Clerk and the City Engineer to
  sign the record map upon completion of any technical corrections required by the City
  Engineer; (2) accepted the off-site improvements constructed in the public right-of-way
  by Target Corporation; (3) authorized the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign the
  Subdivision Agreement with Target Corporation for Tract Map 16877, and accepted
  Subdivision Warranty Bond No. 105459622 in the amount of $498,282.00, posted by
  Travelers Casualty and Surety Company of America, and (4) authorized the City Clerk to
  release Subdivision Warranty Bond No. 105459622 in the amount of $498,282.00, posted
  by Travelers Casualty and Surety Company of America in one year if no claims are filed.

15.  American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009 (ARRA) Street Improvement
  Project (CIP 202/837)

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the
  faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being
  filed with the City; and (4) authorized payment of the final retention 35 days after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.

18.  Second Amendment to the City of Mission Viejo Technical Outsourcing Agreement

City Council Minutes  4  August 16, 2010
   Approved the Second Amendment to the City of Mission Viejo Technical Services
  Outsourcing Agreement with Baker & Taylor.

19.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for June 2010

  Received and filed.

20.  Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report for June 2010

  Received and filed.

21.  Mission Viejo Community Development  Financing Authority (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for June 2010

  Received and filed.

22.  2010 Residential Street Resurfacing--Slurry Seal (CIP 838)

  Awarded the construction contract for the subject project to Roy Allan Slurry Seal, Inc.,
  in the amount of $410,328.00.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

23.  Public Hearing to Consider All Objections to the Proposed Abatement of Weeds on
  Parcels Less than One Acre for the Annual Weed Abatement Program 2010 - Phase 1

  Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Mayor Kelley opened the public hearing at 6:21 p.m. With no requests to speak, Mayor
  Kelley closed the public hearing at 6:22 p.m.

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Ury, to direct
  the Director of Public Services to proceed and perform the removal of weeds in
  accordance with Section 39569 of the Government Code.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

City Council Minutes  5  August 16, 2010
   Council Member Schlicht indicated that she would like to reverse her July 6, 2010, vote
  for the Marguerite Tennis Center (item 28). She is opposed to going out to bid because
  the city does not own some of the property that the parking lot and basketball courts are
  to be expanded upon. She also stated that RJM Design does not have Council authority
  to be negotiating transfers of property or easements and staff has no estimate on costs for
  realigning the parking lot.

  City Attorney Curley announced that under the City Council Rules of Order, she cannot
  reverse her vote but her statements can be outlined in the Minutes of this meeting.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to
  approve the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of July 6, 2010, as presented.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

3.  Technology Services for El Toro Water District

  Director of Information Technology Jackie Alexander presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht asked if the city will store the El Toro Water District data off-
  site in San Diego and if the contract with that firm allows for third party data storage.
  Ms. Alexander responded that the data can be stored at the city or off-site in San Diego
  and those details have not yet been finalized. She also noted that the contract with the
  San Diego provider is strictly for space and the content of the data is not an issue. El
  Toro Water District has indicated that they have approximately 500 gigabytes of data to
  store.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to
  approve draft agreement to provide technology services to El Toro Water District and
  direct the City Manager to finalize the negotiations and the terms of the agreement with
  the District for City Council approval at a future meeting.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

8.  Check Register dated July 2, 2010, in the amount of $2,876,378.60

City Council Minutes  6  August 16, 2010
   Council Member Schlicht asked if the city is taking advantage of the JPIA's pre-payment
  plan for retroactive adjustments. Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative
  Services Irwin Bornstein responded that the discount was only 2% per-year and staff
  feels the city's portfolio will earn more than 2%.

  Council Member Schlicht also inquired about the JPIA’s dues in relationship to claims
  against the city. Mr. Bornstein stated that the dues are linked to the claims for the entire
  pool of participants and he believes the claims are down overall.

  Ms. Schlicht referred to the April payment for legal bills related to her challenge of the
  argument against Measure D. She believes that she won the lawsuit and that the City
  Attorney is gouging and bamboozling the citizens of Mission Viejo.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to
  ratify the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

11.  Check Register dated July 23, 2010, in the amount of $1,335,953.89

  Council Member Schlicht asked for an explanation of the laptop purchased for Council
  Member Ury.

  Mr. Ury noted that each Council Member is issued a computer for work related to their
  position on the City Council. The computer that was provided to him six years ago is
  broken and needed to be replaced.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to
  ratify the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

13.  E-Verify Ordinance

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Ury, to (1)
  adopt Ordinance 10-281 Amending and Restating Ordinance 07-247, as Amended, as Set

City Council Minutes  7  August 16, 2010
   Forth in Chapter 2.80 of Title 2 of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code; and (2) direct staff
  to return at the City Council Meeting of September 20, 2010, with a policy outlining the
  procedures for implementing and enforcing the ordinance.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

16.  2010 CDBG Residential Street Resurfacing (CIP 838)

  Council Member Schlicht asked if the city will be using the REAS slurry seal or the
  newer option. Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon announced that the city has
  switched to the Tire Rubber (TR) modified slurry seal for this year's residential street
  surfacing project.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to award
  the construction contract for the subject project to R. J. Noble Company in the amount of
  $314,480.00.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

17.  Crown Valley Parkway Widening - Cabot Road to I-5 (CIP 795)

  Council Member Schlicht referred to a paragraph in the agenda report which discusses
  potential impacts to Oso Creek. She expressed the same concerns relating to the tennis
  center expansion project and potential environmental impacts along the Oso Creek.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to
  approve the Second Amendment to the agreement with the City of Laguna Niguel and
  RBF Consulting for professional design services for the Crown Valley Parkway/I-5
  Widening Project, including the City of Mission Viejo’s share of additional costs in the
  amount of $36,083.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  8  August 16, 2010
 OLD BUSINESS

24.  Second Amendment to Owner Participation Agreement between the CDA and
  Mission Viejo Associates, LP, Related to The Shops at Mission Viejo

  Special Counsel Celeste Brady, Stradling Yocca Carlson & Rauth, Newport Beach:
  outlined the proposed amendment to the Owner Participation Agreement for the re-
  tenanting of the Saks Fifth Avenue department store space with a new Forever 21 concept
  department store.

  Scott Richardson, Simon Property Group: answered the City Council Members questions
  and described how the new Forever 21 concept store will fit into the changing
  demographics of the mall.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to adopt
  CDA Resolution 10-05 Approving the Second Amendment to the Owner Participation
  Agreement.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

  Council Member Schlicht noted for the record that she welcomes Forever 21 but she is
  not in favor of changing the Owner Participation Agreement. She expressed concern
  with the loss of a retail department store space and stated that the mall will only have one
  traditional department store when it should have four.

NEW BUSINESS

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

25.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

26.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

27.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

City Council Minutes  9  August 16, 2010
 STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

City Attorney’s Report

Council Member Schlicht expressed concern with the work at Turf Lane Park and she asked
what will happen if the city spends beyond the $80,000 settlement agreement with the County.
She also asked why the agreement was not brought before the City Council in open session.

City Attorney Bill Curley stated that the city was not finalizing an offer therefore the Brown Act
does not require the kind of approval that Council Member Schlicht described. He noted that the
agreement became a public document when the City Council voted upon and approved it and the
agreement is publicly available in the City Clerk's office.

City Manager Wilberg announced that he understood the Council's direction was to rehabilitate
and make Turf Lane Park a usable asset for the community and the residents that surround the
area. While $80,000 was an estimate for the park rehabilitation, some of the elements have been
more costly. Mr. Wilberg stated that staff has been operating under the interpretation of the
Council's direction to refurbish the park but since the project will likely cost more than $80,000,
he asked for clarification of the Council’s intent. He asked for Council direction to cease work if
they would like to limit the project to $80,000. Mr. Wilberg announced that the additional costs
would not exceed his $30,000 spending authority.

No action was taken.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

28.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Ledesma

Council Member Ledesma wished everyone an enjoyable summer.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht stated that there is nothing laughable about not sticking to contract
agreements. Contracts are contracts, not suggestions.

City Council Minutes  10  August 16, 2010
 Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury complimented staff on the Pacific Symphony concert in the park. It was
an outstanding event and he and his family had a wonderful time. Council Member Ury noted
that events like this make Mission Viejo the quality community that it is and city staff produce
these programs that benefit the community without necessarily running to the City Council for
approval at every turn.

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness reiterated comments on the fantastic Prelude in the Park event. He
stated that he really enjoyed himself and he looks forward to next year's concert.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley expressed disappointment that she had to miss the Pacific Symphony concert. She
was in Washington State attending her nephew's wedding but she heard many, many positive
comments about the event. She reminded residents that the Symphony in the Cities concert is
sponsored by Target and is made possible through Mission Viejo tax dollars as well. Mayor
Kelley discussed the verbal compliments and thank you notes that she has received on the
installation of exercise equipment along the Oso Creek trail and at Oso Viejo Park. She has
received quite a bit of feedback from people who are using and enjoying the equipment and she
encouraged residents to check it out. Mayor Kelley discussed her attendance at various events
this summer, including the Child Watch program graduation and the celebration that ended the
Library’s SummerREAD program. She thanked Director of Library Services Valerie Maginnis
and the staff who make this program available to children of the community each summer.
Mayor Kelley encouraged residents to mark their calendars for the Readers' Festival on
September 25, 2010, and she reminded residents that the Character Committee provides a free
movie to promote the character quality each month. Casablanca will be screened in the council
chamber on September 19 as a reinforcement of the character quality responsibility. Mayor
Kelley announced that Community of Character quality for the month of August is self control.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:32 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, September 7, 2010, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of September 7, 2010

City Council Minutes  11  August 16, 2010
